One of the turning points in public support for land conservation efforts—and recognizing the magnificence of the Yellowstone region in particular—came in the form of vivid photographs.两个世纪前，"保护自然而非开发自然"对许多美国定居者而言还是个新鲜念头。公众转而支持土地保护努力——尤其是认识到黄石地区的壮美——其转折点之一，正是以生动照片的形式到来的。 CAs an effective Washington operator, Hayden sensed that he could capitalize on the expedition's stunning visuals. He asked Jackson to print out large copies and distributed them, along with reproductions of Moran's paintings, to each member of Congress. "The visualization, particularly those photographs, really hit home that this is something that has to be protected," says Murphy.作为一名精明的华盛顿操盘手，海登意识到他可以借远征那些震撼的影像大做文章。他让杰克逊冲印大幅照片，连同莫兰画作的复制品，分发给每一位国会议员。墨菲说："这些可视化影像，尤其是那些照片，真正让人意识到这是必须加以保护的东西。" DThrough the trip, Jackson juggled multiple cameras and plate sizes using the "collodion process" that required him to coat the plates with a chemical mixture, then expose them and develop the resulting images with a portable darkroom. The crude technique required educated guesses on exposure times, and involved heavy, awkward equipment—several men had to assist in its transportation. Despite these challenges, Jackson captured dozens of striking photos, ranging from majestic images like his now-famous snapshot of Old Faithful, to casual portraits of expedition members at the camp.在整个行程中，杰克逊用"火棉胶法"摆弄多台相机与多种底片尺寸——他须将底片涂上化学混合液，再曝光，并用便携暗房冲洗成像。这种原始技术需要对曝光时间作出有根据的猜测，且涉及笨重不便的设备——得好几个人帮忙搬运。尽管困难重重，杰克逊仍拍下数十张引人注目的照片，既有如如今闻名遐迩的老忠实泉那样的壮丽影像，也有营地里远征队员的随意肖像。 EThe journey officially began in Ogden, Utah, on June 8, 1871. Over nearly four months, dozens of men made their way on horseback into Montana and traversed along the Yellowstone River and around Yellowstone Lake. That fall, they concluded the survey in Fort Bridger, Wyoming.远征于1871年6月8日在犹他州奥格登正式启程。在将近四个月里，数十人骑马进入蒙大拿，沿黄石河行进并绕黄石湖一周。那年秋天，他们在怀俄明州的布里杰堡结束了勘测。 FThough Native Americans (and later miners and fur trappers) had long recognized the area's riches, most Americans did not. That's why Hayden's expedition aimed to produce a fuller understanding of the Yellowstone River region, from its hot springs and waterfalls to its variety of flora and fauna. In addition to the entourage of scientists, the team also included artists: Painter Thomas Moran and photographer William Henry Jackson were charged with capturing this astounding natural beauty and sharing it with the world.尽管美洲原住民（以及后来的矿工和毛皮捕猎者）早就认识到这片地区的富饶，大多数美国人却并未察觉。正因如此，海登的远征旨在让人更全面地认识黄石河地区——从温泉、瀑布到多样的动植物。除了一队科学家，团队还包括艺术家：画家托马斯·莫兰与摄影师威廉·亨利·杰克逊，受命捕捉这令人惊叹的自然之美并与世界分享。 GThe bill proved largely popular and sailed through Congress with large majorities in favor. In quick succession, the Senate and House passed legislation protecting Yellowstone in early 1872. That March, President Ulysses S. Grant signed an act into law that established Yellowstone as the world's first national park. While some locals opposed to the designation, the decision was largely accepted—and Jackson's photos played a key role in the fight to protect the area. "I don't believe that the legal protection would have happened in the timeframe that it did without those images." says Heather Hansen, journalist and author of Prophets and Moguls, Rangers and Rogues, Bison and Bears: 100 Years of the National Park Service.该法案总体颇受欢迎，以压倒性多数在国会顺利通过。紧接着，参众两院于1872年初通过了保护黄石的立法。当年3月，尤利西斯·S·格兰特总统签署法案，将黄石确立为世界上第一个国家公园。尽管一些地方人士反对这一认定，该决定总体上被接受——而杰克逊的照片在保护该地区的斗争中发挥了关键作用。记者兼《先知与大亨、游侠与恶棍、野牛与熊：国家公园管理局百年史》一书的作者希瑟·汉森说："我相信，若没有那些影像，法律保护绝不会在那样的时间框架内实现。" HPerhaps most importantly, the images provided documentary evidence of the park's sights that later made its way to government officials. Weeks after completing the expedition, Hayden collected his team's observations into an extensive report aimed at convincing senators and representatives, along with colleagues at government agencies like the Department of Interior, that Yellowstone ought to be preserved.或许最重要的是，这些影像提供了公园景致的文献证据，后来送达政府官员手中。完成远征几周后，海登将团队的观察整理成一份详尽的报告，旨在说服参议员、众议员，以及内政部等政府机构的同僚：黄石应当被保护。

As is vividly depicted, a crowd of villagers gathers on an arched bridge to watch an exciting dragon-boat race, while two elderly men stand by the riverbank. One remarks with a delighted smile, "How wonderful! The dragon-boat race in our village is livelier than ever."

The drawing conveys a thought-provoking message: traditional Chinese culture is experiencing a remarkable revival in rural areas. Dragon-boat racing, rooted in the Dragon Boat Festival and the memory of the ancient poet Qu Yuan, once faded in many villages. Yet in recent years such events have regained their appeal. On the one hand, the government's rural revitalization and cultural-confidence campaigns have provided funding and guidance; on the other, villagers have come to see traditional festivals not as outdated customs but as precious heritage that strengthens community bonds.

From my perspective, this trend is both encouraging and meaningful. To keep our traditions alive, we should not only hold festive events but also invite the young to participate and innovate. Only in this way can our cultural roots stay vibrant for generations to come.

The weather in Texas may have cooled since the recent extreme heat, but the temperature will be high at the State Board of Education meeting in Austin this month as officials debate how climate change is taught in Texas schools.

自从最近的极端高温以来，得克萨斯州的天气可能已经转凉，但本月在奥斯汀举行的州教育委员会会议上气氛将会十分热烈，因为官员们将辩论得州学校应如何教授气候变化内容。

Pat Hardy, who sympathized with views of the energy sector, is resisting the proposed change to science standards for pre-teen pupils. These would emphasise the primacy of human activity in recent climate change and encourage discussion of mitigation measures.

帕特·哈迪同情能源行业的观点，她正抵制对学龄儿童科学课程标准的拟议修改。这些修改将强调人类活动在近期气候变化中的首要作用，并鼓励讨论减缓措施。

Most scientists and experts sharply dispute Hardy's views. "They casually dismiss the career work of scholars and scientists as just another misguided opinion," says Dan Quinn, senior communications strategist at the Texas Freedom Network, a non-profit group that monitors public education. "What millions of Texas kids learn in their public schools is determined too often by the political ideology of partisan board members, rather than facts and sound scholarship."

大多数科学家和专家强烈反对哈迪的观点。"他们随意 dismissing学者和科学家的毕生工作，认为那不过是又一种被误导的观点，"监督公共教育的非营利组织得州自由网络的高级传播策略师丹·奎因说。"数百万得州孩子在公立学校学到的东西，往往是由党派校董成员的政治意识形态决定的，而不是事实和可靠的学术研究。"

Such debate reflects fierce discussion across the US and around the world, as researchers, policymakers, teachers and students step up demands for a greater focus on teaching about the facts of climate change in schools.

这类辩论反映了美国乃至全球范围内的激烈讨论，研究人员、政策制定者、教师和学生都在强烈要求学校更加重视气候变化事实的教学。

A study last year by the National Center for Science Education, a non-profit group of scientists and teachers, looking at how state public schools across the country address climate change in science classes, gave barely half of US states a grade B+ or higher. Among the 10 worst performers were some of the most populous states, including Texas, which was given the lowest grade (F) and has a disproportionate influence because its textbooks are widely sold elsewhere.

去年，由科学家和教师组成的非营利组织国家科学教育中心进行了一项研究，考察全美各州公立学校在科学课中如何处理气候变化内容，结果仅有不到一半的州获得B+或更高评级。在表现最差的10个州中，包括一些人口最多的州，其中得州获得最低评级（F），但其教材在其他地区广泛销售，因此影响力远超其本身。

Glenn Branch, the centre's deputy director, cautions that setting state-level science standards is only one limited benchmark in a country that decentralises decisions to local school boards. Even if a state is considered a high performer in its science standards, "that does not mean it will be taught", he says.

该中心副主任格伦·布赖恩提醒说，在一个将决策权下放给地方校董会的国家，制定州级科学标准只是一个有限的基准。即使一个州被认为在科学标准方面表现优异，"那也不意味着它就会被教授"，他说。

Another issue is that while climate change is well integrated into some subjects and at some ages — such as earth and space sciences in high schools — it is not as well represented in curricula for younger children and in subjects that are more widely taught, such as biology and chemistry. It is also less prominent in many social studies courses.

另一个问题是，虽然气候变化在某些学科和年龄段（如高中的地球与空间科学）中得到了很好的融入，但在低龄儿童课程以及生物、化学等更广泛教授的学科中，体现得并不充分。它在许多社会研究课程中也不那么突出。

Branch points out that, even if a growing number of official guidelines and textbooks reflect scientific consensus on climate change, unofficial educational materials that convey more slanted perspectives are being distributed to teachers. They include materials sponsored by libertarian think-tanks and energy industry associations.

"I think individuals being able to rent out their second home as a good thing. If it's their vacation home anyway, and it's just empty, why can't you make money off it?" Horn said. partb_options.head: Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–H

options.label: A
options.en: Last year marks the 150th anniversary of a series of Yellowstone photographs by the renowned landscape photographer William Henry Jackson. He captured the first-ever shots of iconic landmarks such as the Tetons, Old Faithful and the Colorado Rockies, on a late 19th-century expedition through the Yellowstone Basin that was conducted by the head of the U.S. Geological and Geographical Survey of the Territories, Ferdinand V. Hayden. The team included a meteorologist, a zoologist, a mineralogist, and an agricultural statistician.
options.zh: 去年是著名风景摄影师威廉·亨利·杰克逊拍摄黄石系列照片150周年。在19世纪末由领地地质与地理调查局负责人费迪南德·V·海登率领的远征中，杰克逊穿越黄石盆地，拍下了大提顿山脉、老忠实泉和科罗拉多落基山脉等地标性景观的首批照片。团队中还包括一位气象学家、动物学家、矿物学家和农业统计学家。

options.label: B
options.en: Two centuries ago, the idea of preserving nature, rather than exploiting it, was a novel one to many U.S. settlers. One of the turning points in public support for land conservation efforts—and recognizing the magnificence of the Yellowstone region in particular—came in the form of vivid photographs.
options.zh: 两个世纪前，"保护自然而非开发自然"对许多美国定居者而言还是个新鲜念头。公众转而支持土地保护努力——尤其是认识到黄石地区的壮美——其转折点之一，正是以生动照片的形式到来的。

options.label: C
options.en: As an effective Washington operator, Hayden sensed that he could capitalize on the expedition's stunning visuals. He asked Jackson to print out large copies and distributed them, along with reproductions of Moran's paintings, to each member of Congress. "The visualization, particularly those photographs, really hit home that this is something that has to be protected," says Murphy.
options.zh: 作为一名精明的华盛顿操盘手，海登意识到他可以借远征那些震撼的影像大做文章。他让杰克逊冲印大幅照片，连同莫兰画作的复制品，分发给每一位国会议员。墨菲说："这些可视化影像，尤其是那些照片，真正让人意识到这是必须加以保护的东西。"

options.label: D
options.en: Through the trip, Jackson juggled multiple cameras and plate sizes using the "collodion process" that required him to coat the plates with a chemical mixture, then expose them and develop the resulting images with a portable darkroom. The crude technique required educated guesses on exposure times, and involved heavy, awkward equipment—several men had to assist in its transportation. Despite these challenges, Jackson captured dozens of striking photos, ranging from majestic images like his now-famous snapshot of Old Faithful, to casual portraits of expedition members at the camp.
options.zh: 在整个行程中，杰克逊用"火棉胶法"摆弄多台相机与多种底片尺寸——他须将底片涂上化学混合液，再曝光，并用便携暗房冲洗成像。这种原始技术需要对曝光时间作出有根据的猜测，且涉及笨重不便的设备——得好几个人帮忙搬运。尽管困难重重，杰克逊仍拍下数十张引人注目的照片，既有如如今闻名遐迩的老忠实泉那样的壮丽影像，也有营地里远征队员的随意肖像。

options.label: E
options.en: The journey officially began in Ogden, Utah, on June 8, 1871. Over nearly four months, dozens of men made their way on horseback into Montana and traversed along the Yellowstone River and around Yellowstone Lake. That fall, they concluded the survey in Fort Bridger, Wyoming.
options.zh: 远征于1871年6月8日在犹他州奥格登正式启程。在将近四个月里，数十人骑马进入蒙大拿，沿黄石河行进并绕黄石湖一周。那年秋天，他们在怀俄明州的布里杰堡结束了勘测。

options.label: F
options.en: Though Native Americans (and later miners and fur trappers) had long recognized the area's riches, most Americans did not. That's why Hayden's expedition aimed to produce a fuller understanding of the Yellowstone River region, from its hot springs and waterfalls to its variety of flora and fauna. In addition to the entourage of scientists, the team also included artists: Painter Thomas Moran and photographer William Henry Jackson were charged with capturing this astounding natural beauty and sharing it with the world.
options.zh: 尽管美洲原住民（以及后来的矿工和毛皮捕猎者）早就认识到这片地区的富饶，大多数美国人却并未察觉。正因如此，海登的远征旨在让人更全面地认识黄石河地区——从温泉、瀑布到多样的动植物。除了一队科学家，团队还包括艺术家：画家托马斯·莫兰与摄影师威廉·亨利·杰克逊，受命捕捉这令人惊叹的自然之美并与世界分享。

options.label: G
options.en: The bill proved largely popular and sailed through Congress with large majorities in favor. In quick succession, the Senate and House passed legislation protecting Yellowstone in early 1872. That March, President Ulysses S. Grant signed an act into law that established Yellowstone as the world's first national park. While some locals opposed to the designation, the decision was largely accepted—and Jackson's photos played a key role in the fight to protect the area. "I don't believe that the legal protection would have happened in the timeframe that it did without those images." says Heather Hansen, journalist and author of Prophets and Moguls, Rangers and Rogues, Bison and Bears: 100 Years of the National Park Service.
options.zh: 该法案总体颇受欢迎，以压倒性多数在国会顺利通过。紧接着，参众两院于1872年初通过了保护黄石的立法。当年3月，尤利西斯·S·格兰特总统签署法案，将黄石确立为世界上第一个国家公园。尽管一些地方人士反对这一认定，该决定总体上被接受——而杰克逊的照片在保护该地区的斗争中发挥了关键作用。记者兼《先知与大亨、游侠与恶棍、野牛与熊：国家公园管理局百年史》一书的作者希瑟·汉森说："我相信，若没有那些影像，法律保护绝不会在那样的时间框架内实现。"

options.label: H
options.en: Perhaps most importantly, the images provided documentary evidence of the park's sights that later made its way to government officials. Weeks after completing the expedition, Hayden collected his team's observations into an extensive report aimed at convincing senators and representatives, along with colleagues at government agencies like the Department of Interior, that Yellowstone ought to be preserved.
options.zh: 或许最重要的是，这些影像提供了公园景致的文献证据，后来送达政府官员手中。完成远征几周后，海登将团队的观察整理成一份详尽的报告，旨在说服参议员、众议员，以及内政部等政府机构的同僚：黄石应当被保护。
